text:
Jakob Chychrun's week was defined by one check. With three minutes left in Ottawa on Nov. 10, he pinched down and drove his shoulder into Nick Cousins, who was briefly knocked unconscious and will miss seven to 10 days. Officials called a major, reviewed it and took it away, and ESPN reported the NHL's Department of Player Safety ruled the hit legal. Senators coach Travis Green called it a head shot. The two were teammates in Arizona, and the fallout has followed Chychrun since.

On the ice, he is Washington's workhorse: 24:24 a night, 13 points in 18 games, eight assists in his last ten. The Capitals out-attempt opponents with him at five on five, though they do slightly better without him. The goals have not come. After a 26-goal season, he has two, shooting 3.6% on 56 shots, and the team has scored 3.7 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice.

That looks like bad luck more than decline. Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd among defensemen last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 92nd percentile for chances from in front of the net. The shots are still coming.
headline: Chychrun's hit, and the season around it
